name: Blog
description: A blog from Markdown posts: renders each post, the index and an RSS feed with its own theme, then publishes them as one Ravi Pages route.

help.usage: ravi blog build --posts <folder> [--title <t>] [--description <d>] [--author <a>] [--lang pt-BR] [--url <https url>] [--footer <f>] [--drafts true]
help.summary: Render the site from the Markdown posts in <folder> and return the files, without publishing.

sections.title: Posts
lines: One .md file per post, at the top of the folder (README.md, files starting with _ and subfolders are not posts). Optional front matter between --- lines: title, date (YYYY-MM-DD), description, tags (comma-separated), slug, draft (true or false).
An optional site.json in the folder sets title, description, author, lang, url and footer; flags win over it. Unknown flags are an error.
The folder must be inside the working directory. Raw HTML in posts is shown as text, links may only be http(s), mailto or relative paths, and every page carries a policy that blocks scripts.

help.summary: Render the site and publish it as one route of the project's Ravi Page (default /blog).
examples: ravi apps run blog publish --execute -- --posts posts --title "Notas"

sections.title: Rules
lines: Publishing is a write: the router asks for --execute.
Every publish renders every post again, so the index and the feed always match the folder. A folder with no posts is refused instead of emptying the blog.
--route is a path below the project home (default /blog); the home / is refused. Posts land at <route>/<slug>.html.
The script can only pass --route, --title and --project to ravi pages ship; the route keeps the project's visibility, which only the operator changes with ravi pages visibility.
